title: Post-port simplifications, then 2.0.1 by one command
objective: Make pplr simpler without changing what it does, from the candidates that critic-rust's second read of ST0001 WP11 commit 3 (fe4b677) left on vc's board, under hv's rule that a change now makes pplr simpler or easier and adds nothing (vc decision 2). Then release the result as pplr 2.0.1 with one command, `bin/devbin release v2.0.1`, the first real run of its `after:`, `bin/devbin post-cut` (vc decision 27).
context:
hv, 2026-11-04: vc has the pen on pplr, cldr and ccusage. All three are to be properly finished this morning, each releasing signed and notarised by one devbin command. pplr's part is this thread. pplr-dc implements it and vc reviews it.

The candidates. Each one preserves behaviour unless it says otherwise:

- `Pair.how` (src/sync.rs) is a `&'static str` over five words: linked, email, linkedin, phone and name. An enum names them once, and the JSON and the report print the same words.
- `Pair.has_inetloc`: `check()` reads it and `matches()` leaves it false, so false means both "absent" and "not read". "Not read" becomes a state of its own.
- `workbook::write` fills Merged's rows by position, while the reader and the styling go by header. It fills them by header too.
- One macOS gate: contacts/mod.rs, handler.rs and icons.rs each test `cfg!(target_os = "macos")` with their own message, beside open.rs's `macos_only(why)`. One helper serves every gate, and every message stays as it is.
- One walker: grep.rs, links.rs and rename.rs each recurse on their own, with different rules for order, dot names and symlinks, each matching the legacy tool it replaced. They share one walk only if it keeps every rule and reads simpler. Otherwise the package records why and is cancelled.
- One picture rule, a divergence that needs hv's ruling: `tree::PICTURES` takes the first file in About/ by name with any picture ending, while `pplr pictures` and the index try the extensions in turn, so a folder with two pictures can give a different one to each. On the live tree on 2026-11-04, none of the 358 About folders with a picture holds two, so unifying the rules changes no output there today.
- The walks pass over a directory they cannot read without a word, where the legacy's `grep -r` and `find` named it on stderr. Saying so is a divergence, and hv's ruling.

wps.title: Pair: how as an enum, and has_inetloc's not-read state its own
wps.objective: Pair.how names matches()'s five ways once, as an enum whose as_str prints 2.0.0's words, and has_inetloc tells not read (None, from matches()) from absent (Some(false), from check()); every reader sees what it saw at 2.0.0 (AC-01.1).

wps.title: workbook::write fills Merged by header, as the reader and the styling do
wps.objective: workbook::write fills the Merged and Contacts sheets by column header, through the column table the reader and the styling use, so a reordered table cannot misfile a cell; the written workbook is 2.0.0's, apart from core.xml's write stamp (AC-02.1).

wps.title: One macOS gate for every command that needs a macOS service
wps.objective: One helper gates every command that needs a macOS service (contacts, handler, icons and open), and each refusal keeps 2.0.0's message and exit code (AC-03.1).

wps.title: One walker for grep, links and rename, or the record of why not
wps.objective: grep, links and rename walk through one walker that keeps each command's order, dot-name and symlink rules, and names each directory it cannot read on stderr (hv's ruling, vc decision 29); or the package records why one walker is not simpler, and is cancelled (AC-04.1).
wps.body:
## The four walks at 2.0.0

| Walk               | Where                                          | Roots                                                                                       | Order                                                                                              | Dot names                                  | Symlinks                                                                           | What it keeps                                                                                  |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| grep               | `grep.rs:134` `markdown_files`, `:145` `walk`  | each top folder of the data root, by `names()`, past dot-named ones; a symlinked top walked | by name: `names()` sorts each folder's names as lossy UTF-8, and each path is joined from its name | entered and kept below the top             | `symlink_metadata`: never entered, and a symlinked `.md` not kept                  | a regular file whose name ends `.md`                                                           |
| links              | `links.rs:219` `markdown_files`, `:243` `walk` | each argument: a file as itself, a folder canonicalised                                     | the folder's own; the caller then canonicalises each path, drops repeats and sorts by bytes        | passed over, file and folder, at any depth | `file_type`: never entered; a symlinked `.md` kept, then canonicalised to its file | any entry but a folder with the extension `md`                                                 |
| rename search      | `rename.rs:309`                                | each `--refs` root, canonicalised                                                           | the folder's own; two callers sort by bytes, and the third rewrites in any order                   | entered and kept                           | `file_type`: never entered, never kept                                             | a regular file with an extension in the caller's list; a folder named in `skip` is not entered |
| rename named_after | `rename.rs:365`                                | the person's folder                                                                         | the folder's own, as `find` meets them, which the dry run lists and the move follows               | entered and kept                           | `file_type`: never entered; kept when its name matches                             | any entry whose name starts with the prefix, kept before its contents                          |

All four read each folder once, take each entry by its own type, and enter only a real folder, never a symlink to one. All four pass over a folder they cannot read without a word (`names()` gives nothing, and each `read_dir` returns). An entry whose type cannot be read is passed over by grep, links and search; named_after still keeps it when its name matches, and does not enter it.

## One walker

`fs::walk(dir, order, visit)` reads a folder once, in name order (grep's, as `names()` sorts) or the folder's own, and shows each entry to the caller's `visit`, which keeps what it wants and says whether to enter it. The walk enters an entry only when `visit` says so and the entry is a real folder, so no caller can follow a symlinked folder. A folder it cannot read is named on stderr, one line each, `pplr: cannot read <folder>: <why>`, and the walk carries on with the exit code unchanged (hv, vc decision 29: a ruled divergence, with its own line in CHANGELOG 2.0.1). Each caller keeps its roots, and its rules go in its `visit`:

- grep: name order; keeps a regular file whose name ends `.md`; passes over a name that is not UTF-8, as joining its lossy name did; enters every folder.
- links: the folder's order; passes over a dot name and does not enter it; keeps any entry but a folder with the extension `md`.
- rename search: the folder's order; keeps a regular file with a listed extension; does not enter a `skip` folder.
- rename named_after: the folder's order; keeps any entry whose name starts with the prefix; enters every folder.

It reads simpler. Four recursions, each with its own read and its own silent failure, become one. The two rules every walk shares are written once: never entering a symlinked folder, and naming a folder it cannot read.

## What changes

The ruled divergence alone: a folder a walk cannot read is named on stderr. Each command's order, dot names, symlinks and what it keeps are 2.0.0's. No golden holds an unreadable folder, so none changes.

## Tests

AT-04.1 pins each command's rules through its own function, on one temporary tree: nested folders, dot-named files and folders, a symlinked folder, a symlinked note, a `skip` folder and a folder with no read permission. Each function's list is checked against the table above: grep's in name order; links' as its caller sorts it; search's and named_after's as sets, since their order is the folder's. The rules part is green at 2.0.0 too, so its red comes from mutants: a walker that enters a symlinked folder, and one that walks grep in the folder's order. A test through the binary holds the divergence: `pplr grep` over a tree with an unreadable folder names it on stderr in one line, still prints the other matches, and exits 0. It is red at 2.0.0's code, which says nothing.

wps.title: One picture rule for the engine, pplr pictures and the index (hv's ruling)
wps.objective: The engine, pplr pictures and the index choose a person's picture by one rule, the first picture in About/ by name (hv's ruling, vc decision 29), and CHANGELOG's 2.0.1 divergences name it (AC-05.1).

wps.title: pplr 2.0.1 by one command
wps.objective: pplr 2.0.1 released by bin/devbin release v2.0.1 alone, the first real run of post-cut: the signed and notarised asset attached, the formula published, and brew upgrade pplr reading 2.0.1 (AC-06.1).
wps.body:
pplr 2.0.1 by one command (AC-06.1). Before the cut, one prep commit carries three fixes to the signer and the release notes:

- The signer reads its three notary credentials by plain assignment before anything is signed, so a missing one refuses by name. ccusage-vc's F1, 2026-11-04: `bin/.devbin/cmd/macos` line 170 passes `$(secret NAME)` inside notarytool's arguments, where `die` ends only the substitution's subshell, so notarytool runs with an empty value and the failure surfaces only as "not Accepted", after signing.
- `require_identity` captures `security find-identity`'s output before matching it, because `grep -q` under `pipe_fail` can lose to SIGPIPE and refuse an identity that is present. And pack's `tar` runs with `COPYFILE_DISABLE=1`, so no `._` entry can reach the asset. Both are cldr-vc's F6, and Cldr's signer already has them. pplr 2.0.0's tarball carries no `._` entry, so the second is a guard.
- An empty credential refuses by name too, before anything is signed (cldr-vc's nit (a), 2026-11-04).
- `secret()` quotes its account, `-a "$USER"`, because native zsh drops an empty word and `-a` would take `-s` as its account. And post-cut's tap pull names what it looked for on each skip branch (no brew, no tap clone), so its last line claims only what ran. Both come from critic-shell on ccusage's copies of these handlers (R1 and R2, 2026-11-04).
- CHANGELOG.md's `## [2.0.1] - unreleased` section, which WP04 opens with the walker's divergence and to which WP05 adds the picture rule's, gets the rest of the release's notes.

Then main is verified in a fresh clone (check all, test all), the boards are committed and frozen, vc holds the slot, and hv runs one command: `bin/devbin release v2.0.1`.

workbook::write places each cell of the sheets the reader reads, Merged and Contacts, by its column's header, as the reader and the styling do, and a written workbook reads back as at 2.0.0.
One helper gates every command that needs a macOS service, and each refusal keeps 2.0.0's message and exit code.

grep, links and rename walk through one walker that keeps each command's order, dot-name and symlink rules and names each folder it cannot read on stderr, one line each, carrying on with the exit code unchanged; or the package records why one walker is not simpler.
The engine, pplr pictures and the index choose a person's picture by one rule, and CHANGELOG's divergences name it.
pplr 2.0.1 is released by bin/devbin release v2.0.1 alone: the signed and notarised asset attached, the formula published to the tap, and brew upgrade pplr reading 2.0.1.
